scenes.tts: Can one signal at the edge of the sheet decide where a border falls?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Lamp at the Front. The dorsal map with a small glowing source at the front edge. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Can one signal at the edge of the sheet decide where a border falls?

scenes.tts: A gradient across the sheet needs a source of position.
scenes.visual: The dorsal map. Below it, an empty plot: level on the vertical axis, front to back on the horizontal.
scenes.narration: A gradient across the sheet needs a source of position.

scenes.tts: Part of it comes from signalling centres at the edges of the sheet.
scenes.visual: Two glowing spots: one at the medial edge, one at the front.
scenes.narration: Part of it comes from signalling centres at the edges of the sheet.

scenes.tts: The cortical hem, at the medial edge, releases Wint and B M P proteins.
scenes.caption: The cortical hem, at the medial edge, releases Wnt and BMP proteins.
scenes.visual: The medial spot labelled cortical hem, Wnt and BMP.
scenes.narration: The cortical hem, at the medial edge, releases Wnt and BMP proteins.

scenes.tts: At the front is a source of a growth factor, F G F eight.
scenes.caption: At the front is a source of a growth factor, FGF8.
scenes.visual: The front spot labelled FGF8. On the plot, a curve that is high at the front and falls toward the back.
scenes.narration: At the front is a source of a growth factor, FGF8.

scenes.tts: Necessary: remove or block it, and look for the loss or shift of what it controls.
scenes.visual: Card one fills: remove or block, look for loss or shift.
scenes.narration: Necessary: remove or block it, and look for the loss or shift of what it controls.

scenes.tts: Sufficient: add it, or add more of it, and look for a structure induced, enlarged or moved.
scenes.visual: Card two fills: add, look for induced, enlarged or moved.
scenes.narration: Sufficient: add it, or add more of it, and look for a structure induced, enlarged or moved.

scenes.tts: In two thousand one, Tomomi Fukuchi-Shimogori and Elizabeth Grove ran both kinds of test on F G F signalling.
scenes.caption: In 2001, Tomomi Fukuchi-Shimogori and Elizabeth Grove ran both kinds of test on FGF signalling.
scenes.visual: On screen: Fukuchi-Shimogori and Grove, 2001.
scenes.narration: In 2001, Tomomi Fukuchi-Shimogori and Elizabeth Grove ran both kinds of test on FGF signalling.

scenes.tts: They used electroporation. Brief electric pulses drive injected DNA into progenitors at a chosen spot.
scenes.visual: An embryo's brain; a needle injects DNA into the ventricle; electrode paddles pulse, and cells at one spot glow.
scenes.narration: They used electroporation. Brief electric pulses drive injected DNA into progenitors at a chosen spot.

scenes.tts: Their readout was the barrel field, one cluster of cells for each large whisker.
scenes.visual: The barrel field rows on the map, matched to whisker rows on a snout.
scenes.narration: Their readout was the barrel field, one cluster of cells for each large whisker.

scenes.tts: Picture F G F eight as a lamp at the front of a room. Cells judge how far forward they sit by how bright it is.
scenes.caption: Picture FGF8 as a lamp at the front of a room. Cells judge how far forward they sit by how bright it is.
scenes.visual: The curve under the map glows like light from a lamp. Three dashed threshold lines cross the curve; where each crosses, a dotted line rises to an area border on the map. A small corner label: working model.
scenes.narration: Picture FGF8 as a lamp at the front of a room. Cells judge how far forward they sit by how bright it is.

scenes.tts: Turn the lamp up. Add extra F G F eight at the front. Which way should the barrel field move?
scenes.caption: Turn the lamp up. Add extra FGF8 at the front. Which way should the barrel field move?
scenes.visual: The lamp brightens; the curve rises. The barrel field holds still. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Turn the lamp up. Add extra FGF8 at the front. Which way should the barrel field move?

scenes.tts: Toward the back. Cells read themselves as farther forward, so each border falls farther back.
scenes.visual: Every crossing slides back along the thresholds, and the borders and the barrel field slide back with them. The working-model label stays in the corner.
scenes.narration: Toward the back. Cells read themselves as farther forward, so each border falls farther back.

scenes.tts: That is what they found. Later work showed F G F eight can act directly on cells at a distance. Cells also respond through the gradients it helps set.
scenes.caption: That is what they found. Later work showed FGF8 can act directly on cells at a distance. Cells also respond through the gradients it helps set.
scenes.visual: Arrows run straight from the lamp to cells near it and far across the sheet; alongside them, a second, inner gradient also responds.
scenes.narration: That is what they found. Later work showed FGF8 can act directly on cells at a distance. Cells also respond through the gradients it helps set.

scenes.tts: Now block the lamp. They used a soluble receptor fragment that binds F G F eight, and probably related F G Fs. Where does the field go?
scenes.caption: Now block the lamp. They used a soluble receptor fragment that binds FGF8, and probably related FGFs. Where does the field go?
scenes.visual: Free receptor fragments mop up the signal at the front; the curve sinks. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now block the lamp. They used a soluble receptor fragment that binds FGF8, and probably related FGFs. Where does the field go?

scenes.tts: Toward the front. More F G F eight moves it back. Less F G F signalling moves it forward. Opposite shifts mark a signal allocating territory.
scenes.caption: Toward the front. More FGF8 moves it back. Less FGF signalling moves it forward. Opposite shifts mark a signal allocating territory.
scenes.visual: The crossings and the barrel field slide forward. Two labels: gain, moved back; less FGF signalling, moved forward.
scenes.narration: Toward the front. More FGF8 moves it back. Less FGF signalling moves it forward. Opposite shifts mark a signal allocating territory.

scenes.tts: One more test. Put a new lamp at the back, far from the first. What should happen?
scenes.visual: A second, dimmer lamp appears at the back edge. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: One more test. Put a new lamp at the back, far from the first. What should happen?

scenes.tts: Near the new lamp, cells read a high level, as if they sat near the front. Part of the pattern repeats there.
scenes.visual: The curve now dips in the middle and climbs again at the back; a new crossing appears near the back.
scenes.narration: Near the new lamp, cells read a high level, as if they sat near the front. Part of the pattern repeats there.

scenes.tts: They found a partial second barrel field, behind the normal one.
scenes.visual: A small second patch of barrels forms near the back of the map.
scenes.narration: They found a partial second barrel field, behind the normal one.

scenes.tts: How far does a border move? A simple model helps. Its numbers are illustrative.
scenes.visual: The curve redrawn as an exponential. On screen: C = C0 e^(-x/λ). Label: illustrative model.
scenes.narration: How far does a border move? A simple model helps. Its numbers are illustrative.

scenes.tts: Let the level fall by the same fraction over each step back. The decay length is the step that leaves a little over a third.
scenes.visual: On screen: λ, the decay length; level falls to about 37% over one λ.
scenes.narration: Let the level fall by the same fraction over each step back. The decay length is the step that leaves a little over a third.

scenes.tts: Double the lamp, keeping the decay length and thresholds fixed. Every border on the sheet moves back by the same distance. That distance is about seven tenths of a decay length.
scenes.visual: Every crossing slides back by one equal step. On screen: shift = λ ln 2 ≈ 0.7 λ, with λ and thresholds fixed, for each border that stays on the sheet.
scenes.narration: Double the lamp, keeping the decay length and thresholds fixed. Every border on the sheet moves back by the same distance. That distance is about seven tenths of a decay length.

scenes.tts: Halve the lamp, and each border moves forward by the same amount. A border pushed past the edge is lost.
scenes.visual: Crossings slide forward by the same step. On screen: halved, the same step forward; a crossing past the edge disappears.
scenes.narration: Halve the lamp, and each border moves forward by the same amount. A border pushed past the edge is lost.

scenes.tts: The equal steps belong to the exponential shape. A straight-line ramp gives unequal steps.
scenes.visual: A straight ramp replaces the curve; doubled, its crossings move by different amounts. Label: shape matters.
scenes.narration: The equal steps belong to the exponential shape. A straight-line ramp gives unequal steps.

scenes.tts: What survives both shapes is the direction, and a graded response to dose.
scenes.visual: Two labels stay on screen: direction, graded dose.
scenes.narration: What survives both shapes is the direction, and a graded response to dose.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: graded signals help place the areas. In our working model, change the dose and the borders slide.
scenes.visual: The rule appears on screen for the first time: position draws the sketch; input finishes it. Beneath it, labelled working model, the map and curve, borders sliding as the lamp dims and brightens.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: graded signals help place the areas. In our working model, change the dose and the borders slide.
